reviews.text: Cons: Every class other than Paladin dies in 3 hits, doesn't matter what hits they are. Oh, and Scares deal half your health and durability regardless of stats. Weapons all have different swing speeds, combo attacks, and that's ONTOP of the combos you unlock from finishing levels for the first time and the variations with different stats on them- this wouldn't matter if it wasn't so painfully obvious that this is a perfectionist game where you're meant to have everything planned out and done before an enemy even swings at you. Everything has durability and WILL break in the middle of battle once you run out of Wizard Oil, so all the loot has this weird "yes it matters but it also doesn't at all" thing going on with it. Overcomplicated combos that then give you more damage if you somehow manage to memorize all the moves and all the progressions and all the literally everything including enemy moves. Enemies can attack and dodge instantanously, rendering any sort of preplanning useless, so all the combo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, parrying, everything just sort of feels random on if it's going to work out or not.... in a perfectionistic speedcore game. Dash attacks do SIGNIFIGANTLY more damage than anything else, and they also stagger enemies, meaning those enemies won't dodge or suddenly attack for enough time for you to get a combo going, but they'll still hit you once that animation's over, so the only working strat seems to be repeatedly ramming into whoever you're going to kill until they explode. Zero metaprogression outside of Helena's bs quests and the one-time-after-beating-levels unlocks. Yes, there's the Sin Level, but it doesn't persist between runs despite the massive Gold Essence cost, making me wonder why it's even there when Gold Essence is the thing that stacks up the most and is only used for opening certain containers and rerolling otherwise... you know, like a meta-currency in literally any other game? "Difficulty" is handled here not only with the usual scaling, but also with spamming hordes in arenas and making certain enemies bigger and "elite", or has them summon more units if not killed immediately, which sometimes just ends a run by virtue of "oops you triggered a scare and got locked into the animation hehe!!!!" or "oh you didn't kill the summoner, death by horde for you!". (Remember, every single one of those enemies can be doing an instant attack, a dodge, or an un-dashable attack, so the perfectionist design of the game just absolutely implodes and you die right there and then unless you're using a sweeping weapon/sweeping combo, but even then, you are GUARANTEED to take hits and armor durability damage even doing that.) Pro: Once you get past all that and start maining paladin, it becomes a slaughter-rush sim like no other, but, actually getting there and staying there without suddenly detonating from a scare and a horde is very unlikely, and with no metaprogression, you're basically just constantly flinging yourself into a meatgrinder until you decide to stop playing. 0/10.

(Had to cut this down a LOT to make it fit 8000 chars) This is a hard one because I want to like this game a lot, but there are too many issues that people aren't talking about because they're either too wowed by the graphics or afraid of being told they have a "skill issue". The thing is though, the complaints I'm about to make exist independent of skill and actually make the game a bit boring if you're good at it. I will change this review to positive if this stuff is addressed, but considering that the game is "content complete" I don't think much will change. I'm also going to keep playing because by the time I realized the game had these problems I was about 30 minutes past the refund window. I want to make it clear that if I could get my money back I would. So first, the good: - Art style is amazing - Sound design/Music is great - Initial impressions are very good - The basic concept for the game and basic game mechanics are mostly sound BUT, there are issues and they fall into two main categories: Variation and Balance. First, Variation: Within 4 runs (~2.5 hours) I had unlocked around 85% of the non-time-gated (xp gates are basically time gates in this game) content, had visited all three zones, and seen every enemy type. I didn't use any guides to do this and deliberately avoided watching videos that would explain the mechanics. This is the equivalent of playing 2.5 hours of Binding of Isaac and unlocking about ~60% of the collections page by my estimation. I mean sure, there's more stuff to get, but this is LIGHTNING fast progression for a roguelite and I wasn't even trying to go quickly. Moreover, there is very, very little variation in content in this game. There are scant few enemy types that mostly behave the same with only about 3 basic archetypes: melee guy who runs at you, summoner, and projectile shooter. None of these are challenging on their own and despite their somewhat different shapes per zone they all blur together due to how the combat works. Elite enemies exist and at the very least provide some challenge, but they have their own issues and outside of halting combat sometimes they affect nothing. The three zones also feel very samey. They're generated by simple grid pieces that have universal shapes but display different skins per-zone. This means the forest doesn't really have, for example, a big room with trees in it, it just has the same general rooms and shapes as the cave and dungeon but with different scenery. There are some decorations, but they aren't substantial. This becomes an issue very quickly on repeat playthroughs because, as with the enemies, everything just blurs together. What about the weapons? Well, they're also very similar. Sure, they swing at different speeds and have different ranges, but aside from that they're pretty much identical mechanically. They all have 95% identical combos, they can all roll any stats, and they are almost all used the same way. Some standouts like the mage gear exist, but even those use the same combos. Armor is, again, samey. It's just stat gear barring a few pieces that add damage to punches and kicks. Pieces can roll magic abilities, but the fact that it's entirely random (Diablo-style) just means that you end up selling most gear after a quick glance because anything but an objective upgrade is a waste of time. I mean, who wants to spend five minutes carefully considering each gear piece when you could be melted in the next room, or have your gear broken? Traits? Almost all numerical. In a non-roguelite adding 10% more <STAT> is okay, but in this game it's largely inconsequential due to permadeath. No real game-changer traits exist unlike most roguelites where a trait/item might totally alter how you play. Unless you want to take something like "cutting legs makes a little ice nova" or get lucky enough to get a permanent decapitation kill perk on your character, it's just stats. But at least it's skill based and tightly-made right? Well... Now, Balance: This game is both very easy and very hard, both for bad reasons. Normal combat can be easily spammed through up until the game starts throwing 5-10 enemies at you at once, then you'll have to use some combos. What combos? Bash-Kick-Thrust-Whirlwind of course. Those other ones? Useless unless they also trigger whirlwind. Due to how much crap is flying at you the only real way to play this game is to be attacking in all directions at once. Fortunately, you can do that very easily with Whirlwind. Unfortunately, that means every other move is basically useless except for parry (which can combo into whirlwind) and certain magic moves (that also do AoE). So it's too easy? No, because eventually you WILL die to something that you either didn't see or had no reasonable way of knowing would kill you. If there are 10 enemies on screen, you might get unlucky and get 100-0'd by overlapping attacks because your whirlwind was 0.1s too slow. You might also get hit by enemy attacks with hitboxes that are WAY too long, some giant enemies have them. My favorite is having multihit obliterate all my armor in 1 second then dying to chip damage. So it's too hard? No, because if you get good gear rolls you will melt everything and your biggest worry will be healing your gear, not your health bar. How far you get in a run is mostly based on whether you rolled good gear. Skill does come into it, but only as a baseline to not get obliterated by zone 2. Whether you actually clear the final zone is almost entirely down to gear because you WILL have a screen full of unreadable enemy swarms and you WILL be taking hits. "But you said the mechanics were good." Yes, but the problem is that the game ignores them too much. It rarely gives you an opportunity to engage with anything besides spam. I [u]want[/u] to do my cool God Hand combo on a wolfman and finish with an uppercut that blasts his body apart like I'm Kenshiro, but if I try to do that I will die to spam. Instead, I whirlwind to hit everyone so I can survive, and continue until everyone is dead or I explode. If I end up with a 1v1, I parry into whirlwind over and over because it's safe and judging hit ranges is a crapshoot. There's a very good game here, but it's hidden by clashing design additions. The combat system wants to be technical and combo-based, but the encounters are designed to be hyperspeed spam-fests. The gear and levelling wants to be Diablo, but the character lifetime is Binding of Isaac. There's a dismemberment system that you completely ignore because trying to aim at speed in combat is an impossibility. This game could shine brightly, but as of right now it doesn't, not to me at least. HOW TO FIX THIS (for dev): - Less enemies at once, but make them more threatening. Make me actually engage with the combos and the mechanics, especially dismemberment. - Give most/all enemies player weapons and let them use them effectively, including blocking/parrying. - Rebalance mage gear for enemy use. - More variation between the areas, and also change the area tilesets based on if they're A/B/C somehow. Right now there are pretty much only 3 zones that feel like one zone, but there could be NINE zones that all feel distinct. - I know you won't cut the stat-stick gearing but add set items that give non-numerical gameplay-changing effects. - Each weapon type should have substantially different combos and combo moves. Basic stuff like bash and kick follow ups being shared is mostly fine, but the rest should be different. - Nerf whirlwind, it's the source of most issues. - Make traits more unique and scale down everything to compensate for less stat bloat. Comments are off because I don't care to get notifications every time some brainrot sufferer posts "skill issue lol" without even reading what I wrote. Instead, I'll take all feedback in the form of free steam points from clown and laughing reacts. Now pay up.

Mortal Sin is a masterpiece of passion. Blood, sweat, and tears pounded tirelessly into shape. It is a beautifully stylized and brutal roguelite with addicting gameplay loop and satisfying combat. So why do I not recommend it? Ignoring the low hanging fruit that is talking about how this isn't everyone's cup of tea, the game commits some mortal sins of its own. The game doesn't use any form of granular upgrade system, which is fine and doesn't disqualify its categorization, but flies in the face of what many people may expect from a roguelite. But that's the easy thing to point out. No, the problem lays deeper still. Let me take you on a journey. A journey that will take us into the very depths of hell. 5 runs behind me, all failed due to things I couldn't possibly have seen coming or a lack of the necessary oomph in my builds that resulted from bad RNG, I didn't feel like playing fair anymore. A blade the height of two men in my hands, this class would carry me to victory. I was sure of it. Invulnerability while using the whirlwind attack, with all the whirlwind combos memorized. Nothing should've been able to stop me. And nothing did. My build broke the power ceiling about halfway through when I got a cumulative 1.5 times multiplier on all the attack raising buffs I'd accumulated thus far. I could tear through any group of enemies, no matter how large, and barely lose anything. Even the 40 enemy spamfest that'd make Destiny 2 blush was no match for the sheer ferocity of my spinning blade. I made it through 3 sets of 5 levels each, 15 brushes with death under my belt, and the final trial lay open to me. I walked in, panicked slightly as I saw this would be a bosses only affair, then steeled my resolve as I went back to spinning. ... ... ... Then I fell into a pit and died instantly. Some may say skill issue, some may say clown behavior, but when your game looks like this you just can't have instakill hazards. Even from above, the skulls on spikes just looked like set dressing for a place that wouldn't look at all out of place in DOOM. But they were, in actuality, instant kill death pits that cannot be survived by any means. In the final level, I might add. This game is first person DMC, DOOM with melee weapons, whatever other comparisons you want to draw. The big thing is that in those games you have checkpoints, save points, backups, and lifelines. This game gives you none of that. There is no saving you from watching an hour of your life instantly vanish into thin air because you walked slightly wrong, or the terrible enemy warning system didn't show you there was somebody blocking your retreat, or any other number of things. If you do intend to play this game, then be ready for two things: Be ready to do a lot of math very quickly. The game doesn't add up the locked in stat bonuses specific gear types have and the bonus stat ups they can roll. Enemies will not wait for you to check if the numbers add up in a way you like. And be ready to silently close the game in rage as you lose an hour of your life to utter nonsense that you could never have seen coming.

Yeaaaaa, gotta rate this lowly. First the game is easy, but it tries to do cheap stuff to kill you. No bueno, instant deduction. Making it hard to see, while "artsy", also just covers up the cheap stuff it'll throw at you. Kinda sad, because there are bright spots, despite being a little easy. Next, what are these classes? You can tell they were an afterthought. The starting class is all you need really. Things like duelist crank up the easy factor exponentially. Some are nice to make the game more challenging, but most turn this into glorified roblock. Lastly, classless dev at times. The things this guy puts out have been disrespectful toward people and honestly it's disappointing. All in all, it's a nice 45 minute jaunt, but loses its steam from being form over function. It's a nice starter game for the dev, but unless there's an attitude adjustment I'm afraid this may be as good as it gets.

各位玩家，很高兴这部作品的官方中文终于上线了，希望你们能喜欢我的翻译风格！ 如果你想提供任何反馈，讨论游戏或者遭遇了bug，可以在此处、steam讨论组以及更新补丁下留言，或者可以选择加入我们的qq群 858496564 一起讨论游戏！ 我会负责中文社区与开发者的沟通，一起帮助我们的游戏变得更好吧！ ————————————————————————————————————— 你说的对，但是《凡人之罪》是由Nikola Todorovic自主研发的一款动作冒险游戏。游戏发生在一个被称作「赦罪之路」的幻想世界，在这里，被本源选中的人将被授予「罪已赦」。导引弹反之力，你将扮演一位名为「苦行者」的神秘角色，在怎么办只有沙的旅途中邂逅温柔体贴说话细声细语的角斗士、菜就多练被举报的海盗、第一男拳的武僧、盾构让人唠一辈子的圣骑士、凡人自己也有✌的法师、害羞可爱转起来叫你欧尼酱的狂战士、吓哭大家的收割者、双刀侠我来给你搓搓背的决斗者、路边开起神秘大排档的猎人、喝口血都能贫血紫砂了的吸血鬼、六边形之一定要活下去啊的苦斗者、至尊平A冲刺冲♿的殉道者、为俺的强大而哭泣吧的咒术师、好像身体被掏空的潜行者、金金金金金金金钱的囤积者、凡人凡人每天早上你醒来的谜影者，和他们一起击败飞舞强敌，找回失散的救赎——同时，逐步发掘「恩尼马蒂克」的真相。 ————————————————————————————————————— 游戏画风奇特，但美术设计和游玩体验非常优秀，同时也有不同视觉风格可供选择，强烈建议在打算正式游玩前浏览画面设置，按照自己的感受修改它可以让你在当前选择的画风内视觉体验更好。 由于是轻度rouge，导致大多数时候你的前几盘都将让你感到有一点吃力，莫名被围殴、突然暴毙、打不出伤害等等，所以我觉得也算一点点类魂吧？（而且我也在翻译文本里藏了一些小彩蛋，如果你游玩过某些作品，你可能会对这些内容感到熟悉，嘻嘻。） 但这些体验都将随着你深入游戏、解锁额外内容、熟悉机制后得到改善，运用格挡与弹反，了解不同的连招衔接，冲撞，踢，平a，技能，前中期解锁的全属性提升得到很好的改善，前期可以先运用自动连招功能无脑平a，但是要想灵活运用，我推荐还是将它关掉。 阅读游戏内的教程，多在初始区域走走，看看地上的小光圈，寻找npc对话，只有只言片语且容易了解，它能帮助你了解游戏的特有机制。（海伦娜你可以理解为防火女，那当地一定就是传火祭祀场罢，随着你的游戏推进与完成任务，她也会逐渐变化外观，并在最后赐予你一把隐藏武器） 总的来说它其实并不是一款完全割草的游戏，但是需要一定的游玩经验与技巧才能逐渐驾驭的（指自信一顿猛冲结果从小缝掉到河里） 苦行者，在每次死亡与轮回后逐渐变强吧！
还是继续玩了几个小时，不应该说是打击手感软绵无力，而是武器挥击时设计的那种慢动作，显得视觉上看上去就很没什么打击感，有一种陷入泥潭的感觉。无法让人欢喜。相比之下，徒手攻击的手感就好上了不少。 如果改一下武器挥击呈现的视觉效果可能会更好一点

一直在进行系统便携化的更新，感觉作者做游戏做的真的很开心，现在普通难度过一轮游戏的体验相当平滑，能不刁难玩家反而不断降低游玩门槛，实在是非常罕见的开发态度。说回游戏本身，真没啥好说的，狂飙的肾上腺素和适度的build内容，砍杀砍杀砍杀砍杀砍杀，永无止境的砍杀，让人感觉自己置身蚀之刻一般的快节奏战斗实在是让人欲罢不能，丰富的职业与武器搭配连段组合技让割草有更强的策略性的同时还做出了职业的玩法分化，保留装备的重复游玩让游戏有像刷子游戏一样的终盘体验，实在是很符合我个人口味的砍杀游戏。

Nice at surface level, until you play a bit more and notice all the flaws. - Class balance is terrible, some classes are so incredibly dogsh*t its not even funny (Warlock) - Has barely any meta progression and at hardest difficulties runs take 40+ minutes so if you die you basically wasted your time - On Torment difficult you can die in less than a fraction of a second, i had a tank run and picked up every single health/defense item i could in the game, a boss killed me in 1 single hit. This coupled with how long the runs take is a serious flaw. Sometimes a Trap can just damage you 10 times in less than 0.25 seconds and instantly kill you i dont know if this is a bug or actually intended at this point. - You basically cannot play this game without constant parrying, and parrying is prompted by a blinking icon appearing on the screen, when enemies are hit, some of them are interrupted, thus removing their Incoming attack parry now blinking icon. This makes it so that sometimes you hit, then you get a parry prompt, you try to parry but your hit stunned the enemy, then you start to attack and the enemy instantly attacks you again, in a big clump of mobs this is complete chaos. - Inconsistent reach: Some weapons have such poor reach it constantly throws you off, you'd think a staff would have longer reach than a dagger? No, the staff is basically a toothpick in range, you have to *literally* stand so close to the enemy you touch their hitbox to hit them with melee attacks. - Useless Combos: Basically every single hold down to spin combo is pretty much useless in 85%+ of scenarios on Torment difficulty, enemies will just swarm you and hit you, thus interrupting you, or just interrupt your charge before it even goes off. Using spin attacks in most scenarios is basically suicide. You're better off never using them, or in Warlocks case where every combo uses the spin: Pick a class that isnt stinking dogsh*t. - Shipwreck level is overtuned and cancerous with hordes of ranged enemies that run away if you go close while spam shooting you and unbreakable cannons that fire everywhere. The bosses are even more incredibly overtuned and will kill you faster than the final boss. - What i think is the worst thing of all is you can *BARELY* tell when a lot of enemies are attacking or not with how much sh*t is on the screen and how their models work, some of them might be flailing their arms and you dont know if its an attack or just moving, i've had times ive died because a enemy TURNED AROUND and it was actually some kind of tail slap attack, but you literally cannot tell the difference. This is comboed with some enemies have 10m reach with their arms, others can only hit whats next to them so you never know if youre standing at a safe distance or you need to parry. - Look at the steam achivement data, most people who play this game play on easy difficulty and probably have Auto Combos enabled so they just run around clicking their mouse. They will not notice these issues. If you are planning on going the Hard difficulty and actually manually doing the Combos you will experience these things i have mentioned in this review. - This is a fun game at its core. But if you make achivements that are only obtainable at certain difficulties i expect those difficulties to be polished, not just flat % dmg/speed/health buffs haphazardly overtuned. Playing for 45 minutes then dying in a split second PoE style without even knowing what killed you while earning nothing because of no Meta progression is not the way to go, the game needs a balance tuning. Edit: I did one final run to get to the actual true end boss, the ''final'' boss had a limb chopped off and stood in the corner of the arena trying to hide and refusing to move, a good 10-20m from the End-game-now-bridge, when i killed the boss i got instantly sucked onto the bridge and wasnt even given an option if i wanted to quit the run or try the boss after or the post endgame challenge. 平心而论打起怪来大部分时间是挺爽的，想爽爽可以入，但很多坑点，想给中评，steam并没有。所以想想还是给个好评吧。 多玩几把就会发现的很多严重搞心态的点： 1.玩家性能是挺强的，但你的陷阱弥补了这一点。你可以把陷阱当成特色，但你不能每个房间都一堆陷阱恶心人，尤其是某些小房间，和特么厕所一样大的地方放个刀片来回转，一个不小心冲刺撞上半条命没了。再搁你屁股后面刷个怪，颇有魂一两狗一羊风范。后期陷阱碰一下半血，地上电锯墙上长矛树上触手之类的还很不起眼。尤其是墙上的大手，还特么是连击，玩家没有受击无敌，一个没注意两巴掌过去能给你满血扇死，快结束了暴毙纯搞心态。它不需要坑你很多次，只要一个没注意杀上头了碰上给你能打暴毙。这么死一次直接给人干红温。打到后面感觉陷阱比很多怪还恶心。 2.这容舟真的是人吗？陷阱最多也是最恶心的图，还给你塞一堆远程小怪，大房间一露头五六条枪线指着你，加上墙上的炮，四个角各占一个枪手墙上一排炮能给你射成筛子，哪都不好躲。这特么还是近战游戏吗？别说能弹反，一人一枪轮流开你就是个靶子，一发没弹到后面给你打出硬直能直接暴毙。你猜鼠疫的魔法之风为什么挨骂？一半原因都是那B牛头弓箭手的锅，近战游戏塞一堆远程怪还很难反制是什么风尚吗? 仿佛又看见了玩圣杯背上插一堆箭被活活射死的画面。老前辈游戏的教训一点不吃。 3.弹反成功没无敌是最难蚌的，弹了一个攻击击退了附近的敌人然后后面手长点的怪上来再给你一刀，受击出个硬直直接断连招。弹反出的无敌来源于给的连击值，不稳定。弹反无敌有，但放天赋里了，这玩意就应该默认有,而不是单纯加连击值提供无敌，连击不够无敌没出你不炸了？也没有受击无敌，还是放天赋里了，我认为这种就应该在基本机制里的，毕竟这游戏节奏很快，很容易出硬直连吃两刀直接暴毙。 4.很多天赋纯凑数，比如踢击火球喝药冲击波啥的，没伤害没生存也没体系，真想不出来这有啥用，污染池子。

I was leaning towards a positive rating until I reached the first big boss and got punished for having the most basic degree of curiosity. Wondering if I could touch the water in this game, I did just that. I was rewarded by losing a weapon and armor piece. Both things I very much needed. That was the tipping for for me. I cannot abide a game that fabricates such egregiously lame artificial difficulty by punishing curiosity and exploration. I acquired a debuff that breaks gear when they run out of mana, so I presume it drained the mana of those items. This would be more or less acceptable if they weren't at the maximum mana values possible. They were full. Pristine. So to go from 100-0 from touching water is just downright stupid. It drained all semblance of joy I had, and made my decision easy. Onto the other flaws. This game is not what it wants to pretend it is. This is not a game that actively rewards learning combos and skill. Enemies spawn all around you, both at the start of, and during, fights. This makes any semblance of tact entirely useless, and braindead AOE skills king. The idea of a first person melee game with combos to learn and enjoy is fantastic, right up until you actually get past the first level and realize the truth of it. No combo will amount to AOEs, especially ones that cover the entire zone. The moment you shatter that very thin pane of glass, you cannot unsee how shallow a pond this game is. The performance is also deceptive. On my 4090, it uses not even 20% of its power to hit 144fps. That changes the moment you fight an actual wave of enemies. Despite 20% of my GPU and 10% of my cpu, or perhaps because of this, my framerate tanks to a whopping 30 the moment I actually start cleaving through a decent amount of enemies. Essentially: When the game finally gets good, the framerate gets bad. It heavily hinders enjoyment. Looting is just the generic +1 or WOW +3!!!! slop where you find marginally better gear throughout, or something utterly gamebreaking with a single AOE. It's not inventive, nor is it very captivating. It's there. In defense of this game in opposition of other negative reviews I saw most, I'm quite confused. Before getting this game, I saw myriad reviews about headaches and qualms with certain visuals in the game. These reviews were very specific about what exactly they had troubles with. It was not the visual style of the game itself, but filters. Filters that the game immediately tells you exactly how to turn off. Given that these reviews were posted the same day I initially played, it was pretty confusing. I also did not like how it looked, but the game gives you all the information needed to turn those off. That's a fantastic bit of QoL, and the reviews complaining about things like the Blur, Grain, Saturation, etc are either intentionally misleading or simply idiotic. Overall, this game is the pinnacle of "Just fine." I think 15$ is a fair price for this. 20$ on sale is pushing it. 25$ without is just laughable. If the combos actually mattered, if the combat had the depth this pretends it does, or if the dungeons weren't the single most basic implementation of procedural generation possible, then maybe...but that's just not the case. It's something to do. Bored? Sure, why not. Play a round or two. But gods forbid you get a tad curious. You will be punished.

When you play this game, you will feel that there are many things that feel "off" with the game design. The combo system doesn’t make any sense. You have a kick move, in games like Dark Souls or Chivalry 2, the kick is a weak attack that can break shield blocking. In this game, the kick is supposed to chained with all the attacks types to form combos, like in fighting games like Mortal Kombat or Street Fighter. Some enemies can kill you in one shot in the easiest difficulty, and I’m not even talking about the final boss, why ? That never happens in Binding of Isaac nor in Hades. Let’s talk about the sin remnants feature. At the end of a run, you can choose to keep a bonus for the next run, but only if you start the next run immediately. If you dare to quit the game, the bonus is lost. Why incite players to chain runs in a world where video game addiction is a real issue ? The problem in this game is that the developer wants the player to play frenetically, he wants you to mash the buttons, and he wants you being overly frustrated until you beat the damn game. That’s not the same thing as harsh difficulty, and this is coming from somebody that liked Sekiro and Ghostrunner. I’m sorry, but I am a player, I am not a junkie.

I think I have to agree with some of the negative reviews. The game looks great, has it's own style going for it, but feels like an utter mess to play. It's not all bad though. The can be snappy and fun in little bits. The dodges, kicks and everything seem fine, there's a few fun classes to spam abilities with and lots to unlock. The dismemberment in combat is ridiculous in the best of ways, legless and armless zombies trying to attack you. And sometimes the feeling of mayhem is spectacular, when you are whirlwinding through tons of enemies. Enemies are spastic, nothing really feels like it has impact so you just spam away, using the best combo you can to whittle away at the enemies. The combat is fun for a while, but it's just so damn messy with enemy attacks coming from where ever. Not once or twice have I been slapped around way too hard by a zombie spawning behind me, or having a floor effect kill me with little warning. Those weren't cool in Path of Exile or Diablo, and they aren't here. I guess the game wants you to experience the wonders of discovering things on your own, but some of the systems (at least were) really opaque. The game takes you to places and throws things at you, and you just have to guess at what it all means, or read a wiki. I also really, really hate most of the traps, with a special mention to the forest level branches and hands. The buzzsaws are fine, they are readable and avoidable, but the swinging branches and such actively drain joy from the game. I'd pick Vermintide over this almost any day.

The combat feels ill-paced and floaty. There is little feedback for when you land hits, and enemies tend to feel very clumsy (not to mention yourself). The parrying doesn't feel impactful and enemy attacks are able to be interrupted as the parry symbol is going off, resulting in you throwing an attack, then realizing you should be trying to parry, and then realizing that you hit the enemy and interrupted them, and then realizing that you should try to keep attacking, but now the enemy is already attempting to swing again- and you get the idea, I'm sure. Complete breakdown of the flow of combat... not that there really was a "flow". Most of it boils down to trying to throw out as many combos as you can before the enemies get an opportunity to hit you with something. The combos feel arbitrary and pointless. A large array of things that do what? I'm not sure, it's poorly described. You just press some buttons and things happen. The traps are also absurd. Any of the spiked traps are pointless, and the meat-people inside the wall are hellbent on killing you. I have only played on the hardest difficulty, but if the only thing that entails is an enemy health/damage-engorging, as it seems, then I'm not really interested in playing on the lower ones.

TL;DR: Do you like high octane FPS roguelike dungeon crawlers? Yes? What about DDR/Rhythm based input for combat and by extension, combos? Now what if your level of skill and progression in this game is determined by how well you can essentially treat your keyboard like a game of DDR or Guitar Hero WHILE playing a game geared toward and skinned as something akin to Roboquest, Hades, Voin, Barony, etc.? If your answer ultimately ended in no, you will not like this game. The very choice of how combat is handled is what alienated me, and what would turn most people off from this game. Everything else is a win in my book, but unfortunately the core mechanic cannot be altered.

In the sea of roguelike games, this one doesn’t stand out in any meaningful way. It feels as if it’s held together by duct tape. The experience is extremely chaotic and overly reliant on a poorly implemented combo system. Combat feels weightless and becomes repetitive quickly. Randomized loot is handled in a dull way and feels pointless. There are also plenty of annoying mechanics, like scares or those portals that lead to small platforming sections (which are horrid). Progression feels aimless and poorly structured. Mortal Sin first released in Early Access in March 2023, and after more than three years it still doesn’t seem to have found a cohesive vision. It’s a mess of ideas that probably seemed cool in the solo developer’s head, with no one around to challenge them. At this price point and with so many better games available I’d say give this one a pass. If you’re skeptical, just look at the Global Steam Achievement stats: only 5% of players have completed a full run with any class, and most seem to have dropped off after barely progressing into the game.

在新版本更新之后我又玩了几个小时苦痛之路，最终决定卸载。允许任何人喷我菜。 其一，新出的非常巨大的骑士给我一脚踢死好几次了，我没见过一个比玩家角色还全面的怪物。不论是防御还是血量还是远近切换的攻击都远远在玩家性能之上，光是0帧起手的光波就给我弄死好几次，更别说超级无敌铁血格挡了。 其二，陷阱好像变得更多了，无疑是十分难以理解。尤其是在洞穴关卡，凹凸不平的地表配合陷阱极其容易在怪多的时候卡脚卡死。 其三，关于关卡中跟随某个角色的任务我觉得是最弱智的设计，狭窄的范围让人根本不能离开半步，而且有的角色跑起来飞快，标志的圈在一堆特效和血浆中根本注意不到。角色的实体设计更是恶心，不能想象一个移动木桩时刻都在阻挡你的攻击，还不能阻挡怪物的攻击。 我本来觉得是自己菜的问题，后来发现根本没必要再花时间玩这个破游戏。

This game gets a bare pass. It's fine. It's mechanically extremely repetitive and boring. It uses a colour coding system for the combos that make it basically impossible to play if you stop playing, kind of like the colour coding they use for Xbox controllers because the buttons are actually that colour, so it makes logical sense in that case. When criticized about this obvious glaring design issue, and given the suggestion that the yellow circle that represents "attack" should communcate the function rather than an abritrary colour scale, I was banned from the discord. I'll try not to let this effect my review moving forward. This is a first person roguelite with fighting game elements. You enter your fighting game combos out of a combination of three inputs - Attack, dash and kick. There are various classes that have different combos, and a shuffle mode to keep your combo list moving and varied. A wide variety of weapons, enchantments and roguelite run buffs enhance your character. Your eventualy goal is to clear 3 levels. The levels get progressively harder and have variants based off when you do them. So if you do the forest 3rd, it is scaled up to be a tier 3 dungeon. If you do it first, it's pretty easy. I basically described the entire game in that one paragraph. There isn't any nuance or anything unique about the game. The art style is garish even in the "realistic" mode that the developer had to make because he was getting such bad reviews. The story is basically a non event and is somehow pretentiously written, but also under written. There's a half naked angel and you're on some kind of path of redemption or something. It's presented to you exclusively through text and doesn't dwell on the story so I won't either. It's just there in my review like it is in the game. Ultimately, it just comes across as a student project. It lacks the care and precision of professional work. The animations look kind of dumb and it is extremely repetitive. If you're not the type of person who is amused by lots of colours on the screen you'll quickly realize you're mostly just pressing the same 3 buttons over and over and over and playing with the exact items your chosen class demands you to play with. In an attempt to feign difficulty the player agency was just basically removed. There is no balancing done as well so a lot of the time the best option is just to use power attack or the spin attack repeatedly because adding a kick or a dash would just lower your DPS, and the combo doesn't pay out for it's time investment in the vast majority of cases. Like the original art style, the gameplay itself was just poorly concieved, is as wide as the ocean but about as deep as a puddle, and is just an inferior version of things that are already on the market. If you're on the fence, I think you should grab it. Play it for 3 hours and then return it if you don't like it. It's one of those games. If you've looked at the store page and thought; "That looks a little bit ♥♥♥♥...", the feeling doesn't go away when you play it like some indie games, which is why it doesn't get a recommend. Even when you get into the flowstate in this game, which it seems to expect you to do, you're constantly tripping over dead frames and animations that have to play out and it never feels like you're in full control. It doesn't have a good gamefeel, well written characters, soul or anything particularly endearing about it, and if you want my personal opinion, I think it was made by a pretentious little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can tell by the snyde nature of the post that said he added realistic mode for all of the people who didn't "Get his original vision". A lazy, self professed artist who's best work is embarassing when put next to an actual artist, failing upwards by copying other people's work and not really contributing very much overall. It only gets a passing grade because the games he copied were fantastic and the bulk of the criticism of this game from all sources, not just me, is the stuff he did himself. Again. He had to remake all of the art because it was awful but he thought it was good. That's what we're dealing with. It's better to just give your money to someone who is going somewhere rather than some kind of airhead with delusions of grandeur. Please refer to my Caves of Qud review if you think I don't give recommends to titles when I've conflicted with the developer. If this was an amazing game I would recommend it regardless but it just isn't. It's good enough, which is the exact effort that was put into most aspects of this title. It's technically a game and it technically has all of the parts there, but it's a pale imitation of actual art.
